what the testbench measures, and what it refuses
Measured on the PADS, in CLOCKS.
1. every cell on the 75-clock grid: the rising edge is at t0 + 75k EXACTLY
4. every 1 still HIGH at the strip's sample point (+42 clocks)
5. reset > 50 us before frame 1 AND between frames
6. n_released == 0 - the line is never released
7. non-vacuity: cell 0 is a 1, the frame has both bit values, it repeats
Why equality and not a window:
47 or 49 clocks is 783 or 817 ns and
clears every datasheet window. But a cell that is 74 clocks shifts every
sample in the frame, and a byte-boundary path one clock longer stretches
three cells in every frame - a frame 3/24 wrong, which no window check can
see and a strip absolutely can.
